assets.article_title: US Grid Constraints: Towards 40GW+ of Behind-The-Meter Datacenter by 2028?
assets.credit: SemiAnalysis Energy Model (in-image credit); article caption adds SemiAnalysis Datacenter Model.
assets.article_caption: Source: SemiAnalysis Energy Model, SemiAnalysis Datacenter Model
assets.data_date: Analyst model vintage as of article publication, 2026-06-25 (asset Last-Modified 2026-06-25 18:00:31 GMT); no separate data date stated
limitations: Analyst model forecast, not a measurement. All five bars, including 2026, are SemiAnalysis projections from proprietary models that are not public.
Annual net additions (GW added in each year), not cumulative installed capacity. Do not sum the bars on the slide or read 84 GW as the 2030 US datacenter fleet.

The blue series is a residual: modeled datacenter demand minus modeled grid headroom and new grid supply, i.e. the shortfall the article says must be filled behind the meter. It is not a count of announced, permitted or contracted onsite generation projects.

Title says 'Gross DC MW' but the axis and data labels are in GW. 'Gross' is facility-level datacenter power demand (article: 'Gross Power Demand'), not critical IT load; the public text does not define it further.

The chart subtitle says 'towards 50GW+ by 2028' while the article title says '40GW+ by 2028' and the 2028 blue value is 42.6 GW; blue first exceeds 50 GW in 2029 (52.4). Quote the bar values, not the subtitle.

The public text does not explain how 'New Grid Supply' (1.9, 9.5, 11.1, 13.6, 18.3 GW) is derived from the article's ~15 GW/yr net new ELCC capacity figure, nor how much is reserved for non-datacenter load. 2026 blue (~1.8 GW) and green (~1.9 GW) values are unlabeled and were read from pixel heights.
Preserve the source legend, in-image credit and watermark. Display as a dated analyst forecast.
